title: Finite-basis tensor evaluation, exactness detection and the termwise complex comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, with terminal object $1$, and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and restriction $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Suppose $d\geq0$ is finite and $b_i\in S(1)$ give an isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi S$, $(r_i)\mapsto\sum_i\varphi(r_i)b_i$. Denote its inverse coordinates by $q_i:S\to R$, and write $b_i|_U$ for restriction to any site object $U$.

For every $R$-module sheaf $F$, put $T(F)=F\otimes_R S$, with the sheafified tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The presheaf $U\mapsto F(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)$ is already a sheaf. There are natural inverse $R$-module sheaf isomorphisms
$$\Phi_F:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi T(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{\oplus d},\qquad\Phi_F([f\otimes a])=(q_i(a)f)_i,\qquad\Phi_F^{-1}((f_i)_i)=\sum_i[f_i\otimes b_i|_U],$$
where brackets denote the sheafification unit. For every $U$ the canonical map
$$\theta_{F,U}:F(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(F)(U),\qquad f\otimes a\longmapsto[f\otimes a]$$
is an $S(U)$-linear isomorphism. It is the identity between the two coordinate copies of $F(U)^d$, and its inverse sends $x$ to $\sum_i(\Phi_{F,U}(x))_i\otimes b_i|_U$. The comparison is natural in $F$, commutes with restriction in $U$, and is independent of the basis: it is uniquely determined by its displayed pure-tensor formula.

Restriction of scalars along any $\varphi$ preserves kernels and cokernels and preserves and reflects exactness. Under the finite-basis hypothesis above, $T$ is additive and exact. For any homomorphism of ordinary commutative rings $A\to B$ with a finite $A$-basis of $B$, ordinary scalar extension $N\mapsto N\otimes_A B$ is also additive and exact. Here exactness means preservation of finite limits and finite colimits, and a composable pair is exact precisely when its image equals the following kernel.

For every possibly unbounded cochain complex $K$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], the maps $\theta_{K^j,U}$ give a natural isomorphism of cochain complexes $K(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)\cong (K\otimes_R S)(U)$, with termwise tensor differential. Its inverse has the preceding coordinate formula in every degree.

proof.text: Evaluate the given basis isomorphism using Mathlib evaluationPreservesFiniteLimits and PreservesProduct.iso. ModuleCat.piIsoPi identifies its finite product with coordinate functions, including the empty family. The inverse coordinates are linear and commute with restrictions because they are components of e.inv followed by the coordinate projections. These are constructions in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tags 03DA and 03DB, lemma-abelian and lemma-limits-colimits; finite-product coordinate calculation

proof.text: Write $P_F(U)=F(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)$, with $S(U)$ acting on the second factor, as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The map $(f,a)\mapsto(q_{i,U}(a)f)_i$ is additive in each argument and balanced, since $q_i(\varphi(r)a)f=q_i(a)(rf)$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore defines an $R(U)$-linear map $\beta_U:P_F(U)\to F(U)^d$. Define $\gamma_U((f_i))=\sum_i f_i\otimes b_i|_U$. On a tuple, $(\beta_U\gamma_U(f_i))_j=\sum_i q_j(b_i)f_i=f_j$. On a pure tensor, $\gamma_U\beta_U(f\otimes a)=\sum_i q_i(a)f\otimes b_i=f\otimes\sum_i\varphi(q_i(a))b_i=f\otimes a$. Pure tensors generate, so these are inverse maps on all elements.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, universal property and generation; applied to the presheaf tensor of Tag 03EK

proof.text: For $V\to U$, the two restrictions of $\beta_U(f\otimes a)$ both give $(q_{i,V}(a|_V)(f|_V))_i$; restriction of $\gamma_U((f_i))$ gives $\sum_i(f_i|_V)\otimes b_i|_V$. Thus $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are inverse maps of $R$-module presheaves. A matching family for $P_F$ is carried by $\beta$ to $d$ matching families for $F$; glue each coordinate in $F$ and apply $\gamma$. Uniqueness holds coordinatewise. Hence $P_F$ is already a sheaf, including for empty covering sieves, and its existing semilinear $S$-action makes it an $S$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. In Lean, prove finite-product section extensionality directly by evaluating product coordinates, and use the defining pure-tensor equation of changeOfRingsMap for restriction compatibility. These local helpers work with the independent site universes and require no small-site scalar-extension theorem.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; coordinatewise verification of the sheaf condition

proof.text: Let $\eta:P_F\to T(F)$ be the module-sheafification unit of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with the ring presheaf already equal to the ring sheaf $S$, using $S\to S$ as its sheafification. Since $P_F$ is a sheaf, the identity of $P_F$ factors uniquely as $\epsilon\eta$ for an $S$-linear sheaf morphism $\epsilon:T(F)\to P_F$. Then $\epsilon\eta=1$, and $\eta\epsilon=1$ by uniqueness after precomposition with $\eta$. Consequently $\Phi_F=\beta\epsilon$ and $\Phi_F^{-1}=\eta\gamma$ are inverse $R$-module sheaf morphisms, with precisely the two displayed formulas on $[f\otimes a]$ and on $(f_i)$.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules (factorization and uniqueness); Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product

proof.text: The component $\eta_U$ is exactly $\theta_{F,U}$ and is $S(U)$-linear, with inverse $x\mapsto\sum_i(\Phi_{F,U}(x))_i\otimes b_i|_U$. Moreover $\Phi_{F,U}\theta_{F,U}=\beta_U$, so in the two coordinate copies of $F(U)^d$ this map is the identity. For a module sheaf map $h:F\to G$, both composites in its naturality square send $f\otimes a$ to $[h_U(f)\otimes a]$; tensor generation gives equality. For restriction along $V\to U$, both composites send $f\otimes a$ to $[(f|_V)\otimes(a|_V)]$. The defining map $\eta_U$ has no basis in its pure-tensor formula, and two linear maps with that formula agree by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This proves the asserted naturality, restriction compatibility and basis independence.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, sheafification-unit comparison; uniqueness from algebra Tag 00CX

proof.text: For arbitrary phi, the additive restriction functor of [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] followed by toSheaf R is definitionally toSheaf S. The forgetful functors of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] preserve finite limits by Mathlib and finite colimits by the proved instance SheafOfModules.preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Sheafification. They reflect isomorphisms, hence reflect finite (co)limits. The composite preservation/reflection criterion therefore proves finite exactness of restriction directly.

proof.text: An equality imageSubobject f = kernelSubobject g implies f ≫ g = 0: factor f through its image and use Subobject.ofLE for the equality to factor through the kernel. Apply this also to the restricted pair and use faithfulness to reflect the zero composite. Form the corresponding ShortComplex. Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_iff_image_eq_kernel, exactness preservation by an additive finite-exact functor, and reflects_exact_of_faithful give the required equivalence without any a priori complex hypothesis.

proof.text: In the abelian category [def-sp-abelian], identify the finite power with Functor.const (Discrete (Fin d)) followed by lim. Both factors preserve limits. Finite biproducts identify lim with colim by HasBiproductsOfShape.colimIsoLim; Functor.const and colim preserve finite colimits. Transport preservation across these natural isomorphisms. This also covers d = 0.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, kernel/cokernel criterion; finite coordinate factorization in an abelian category

proof.text: The ordinary extension/restriction adjunction makes scalar extension additive, so sectionwise tensor is additive. Module sheafification is additive because it preserves binary products. Thus the explicitly constructed composite E is additive. The already-sheaf result makes the module sheafification unit an isomorphism, and its inverse composed with tensor coordinates gives the natural isomorphism E ⋙ Res_phi ≅ finitePower. Step 8 and transport along this isomorphism show finite exactness of E ⋙ Res_phi. Step 6 and reflection of isomorphisms by restriction show restriction reflects finite (co)limits. The composite preservation/reflection criterion proves finite exactness of E.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; agent finite-basis consequence using homology Tag 010N

proof.text: For ordinary commutative rings A → B, the specified finite basis gives a free A-module structure on B, hence flatness. Mathlib ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat gives finite-limit preservation. The extension/restriction adjunction gives finite-colimit preservation and additivity. This proves the same ordinary-module conclusion directly, without constructing the one-object site.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, specialized to the one-object identity site

proof.text:
Let $K$ be any cochain complex as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Additivity of $T$ makes its termwise differentials square to zero. In degree $j$, use $\theta_{K^j,U}$. For $f\in K^j(U)$ and $a\in S(U)$, both sides of the differential-compatibility equation are $[d^j_U(f)\otimes a]$:
$$\theta_{K^{j+1},U}(d^j_U\otimes1)=(T(d^j))_U\theta_{K^j,U}.$$
Tensor generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extends this equality to every element. The inverse degreewise maps are those of Step 5, and the same equation after composing with inverses makes them a chain map. Naturality in a chain map follows degreewise from Step 5; restriction compatibility holds likewise. All formulas involve one degree at a time, so no boundedness, infinite sum or totalization is used.

theorem basedSheafTensorEvaluation :
    (∀ (φ : R ⟶ S),
      PreservesFiniteLimits (restrictScalars.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map φ)) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (restrictScalars.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map φ)) ∧
      ∀ (M N P : SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj S))
        (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P),
        (imageSubobject f = kernelSubobject g ↔
          imageSubobject ((restrictScalars.{u}
            ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map φ)).map f) =
          kernelSubobject ((restrictScalars.{u}
            ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map φ)).map g))) ∧
    (∀ (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
      (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) A
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).obj (ModuleCat.of B B))),
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} φ).Additive ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} φ) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, u} φ)) ∧
    ∀ (one : C) (hOne : IsTerminal one) (φ : R ⟶ S) (d : ℕ)
      (b : Fin d → S.obj.obj (op one))
      (e : (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin d ↦
          unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ≅
        (restrictScalars.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map φ)).obj
          (unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj S)))
      (he : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (r : Fin d → R.obj.obj U),
        e.hom.val.app U
          ((basedTensorProductSections d
            (unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) U).inv r) =
          ∑ i : Fin d, φ.hom.app U (r i) * S.obj.map (hOne.from U.unop).op (b i)),
      ∃ E : SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R) ⥤
